part.text:
The fix is complete. Following the upstream resolution for this issue (tokio-rs/tokio#4384), I added explicit `UnwindSafe`/`RefUnwindSafe` implementations for the internal `PollEvented` wrapper in tokio/src/io/poll_evented.rs:9,216:

```rust
use std::panic::{RefUnwindSafe, UnwindSafe};
...
impl<E: Source> UnwindSafe for PollEvented<E> {}

impl<E: Source> RefUnwindSafe for PollEvented<E> {}
```

Because `UnwindSafe`/`RefUnwindSafe` are auto traits, an explicit impl overrides the compiler's structural derivation, so the interior-mutable internals (`UnsafeCell` in the slab, `ScheduledIo`, driver mutexes) no longer prevent the wrapper — and thus `net::UdpSocket`, `TcpStream`, `TcpListener`, `TcpSocket`, `UnixStream`, `UnixListener`, and `UnixDatagram` — from crossing a `catch_unwind` boundary. This is sound: those cells are never mutated through `&` references while panics unwind (panic unwinding never grants mutation access through the shared `Registration`/`PollEvented` refs).

Verification:
- `cargo test --test net_types_unwind` — both tests pass (previously failed to compile with 24 E0277 errors)
- `cargo test -p tokio --features full --lib` — 116/116 pass
- Net-related suites (`udp`, `tcp_stream`, `uds_stream`, `net_bind_resource`, `async_send_sync`) all pass

The only failing test, `tcp_socket::basic_usage_v6`, is a pre-existing environmental failure (`AddrNotAvailable` — the container lacks the required IPv6 address) and is unrelated to this change.
